entries.english: Since, through human negligence and the passage of time, many human deeds fall into oblivion, wiser counsel has decreed that reasonable acts be committed to the memory of writing and passed on to posterity. Let all present and future people know that we, Witigo and our brother Wok, sons of Lord Wudwoii of blessed memory of Krumau, while still fully able to dispose of our affairs and wishing to exchange temporal things for eternal ones, have freely and without anyone’s objection given to the house of Saint Mary ever Virgin at Hohenfurt, our foundation and that of our friends, three hereditary villages of ours: Ulrichsschlag, Klein-Drasen, and Hohenschlag, with all their appurtenances and rights, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated fields, pastures, roads and tracks, woods, groves, mountains, valleys, waters, fishing, hunting, and defined boundaries. We give them to be held in perpetuity for the remission of our sins and those of our other relatives, for the salvation of the soul of our beloved brother Zawis, and to restore the spiritual benefit due to him, which had not yet been fully paid because of negligence. The abbot of the aforesaid house shall devote these villages to the uses of his church as he knows will best serve him and the brothers serving God there. To make this gift firm and free of future challenge, we have given this sealed charter to the brothers at Hohenfurt, who pray to God for us. Witnesses, in addition to our paternal uncle Heinrich von Rosenberg: Thsenko and Andreas, knights; Wisconis, Ulrich, and Thsedworii, brothers of Weihseln; Qualonis of Sheztav; and many other worthy men whose names are omitted for brevity. Given in 1290. The fine, rather large, well-preserved white wax seal probably once hung from silk threads. It shows a triangular shield with a five-leaved rose under a helmet bearing a rose ornament; the inscription reads “Seal of Wi...go of Krumau.” Reference: Millauer, p. 98, no. 21.
